subject: Day 33: serve-and-return coos
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi is 33 days old and starting to make vowel sounds and eye contact during feeds. The day's high-leverage habit is serve-and-return: turn his coos into full back-and-forth exchanges, since conversational turns predict later language outcomes more than raw word volume.

Action items
- Build full coo conversations several times today: respond to his vowel sound, pause two to three seconds, wait for his next one, then respond again; turn count, not word count, is what tracks with later language-related brain function. Romeo et al. 2018, conversational turns and brain function: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Make deliberate eye contact during feeds and let his social smiles consolidate as he quiets to your familiar voice; these are the developmentally on-track markers to expect this week. AAP Bright Futures tools and resources: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Help Anoushka draft pre-visit notes for the 6-week postpartum appointment now: pelvic floor symptoms, mood, contraception, and the return-to-work date; ACOG advises rescreening mood at that visit and messaging the OB sooner if symptoms are escalating.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Quieting to a familiar voice and brief eye contact during feeds; these are expected gains, not concerns, in week 5.
- [monitor] No emerging social smile and no quieting to your voice by eight weeks; document it now and flag it at the 2-month visit.
- [call within 24h] A cluster of new symptoms together, such as poor feeding plus unusual lethargy plus decreased wet-diaper output.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea or a color change, or seizure-like activity; do not wait on any of these!

Enrichment opportunities
- Run serve-and-return coo exchanges throughout the day: respond, pause, wait for his vowel sound, respond again. This bidirectional pattern, not passive talking, is the mechanism behind language growth. Romeo et al. 2018, conversational turns and brain function: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Hold steady eye contact during feeds and reward each social smile with one back; the face-to-face loop is consolidating his social-emotional circuitry this week. AAP Bright Futures tools and resources: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Take a 20 to 30 minute daylight stroller walk for varied sensory input and Anoushka's cardiovascular recovery; keep giving the 400 IU per day vitamin D drop regardless of time outdoors. AAP HealthyChildren: Vitamin D On the Double: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 35-41 (around week 6): Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit; bring the written questions on pelvic floor, mood, exercise, and contraception.
- Day 56-70 (2-month well visit): six vaccines due, including the first oral rotavirus dose.
- Day 57-72 (post-vaccine window): expect 24 to 48 hours of fussiness and low-grade fever after the shots.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
